description: Spain puts its own conquests on trial: Sepúlveda's natural-slavery argument against Las Casas's eyewitness testimony. No verdict — but the question survived.
essential_question: Could the conquest of the Americas be morally justified?

key_terms.definition: The 1550-51 council debate at Valladolid, Spain, over whether Spain's conquest of the Americas was just.
Spanish theologian who argued from Aristotle that Indigenous peoples were natural slaves and conquest was a just war.
Dominican friar whose fifty years in the Indies grounded his eyewitness case that Indigenous peoples were rational and Spanish cruelty was the true barbarism.
Sepúlveda's Aristotelian claim that some peoples are born to be ruled.
The idea first articulated at Valladolid that conquest itself can be judged by universal moral law.

learning_objectives: Summarize Sepúlveda's argument from natural slavery and its Aristotelian roots.
Explain Las Casas's defense of Indigenous peoples, including his tragic early irony.
Evaluate why the debate changed little on the ground but mattered for the history of rights.

presentation.tone: a teacher talking to a smart 16-year-old; plain, spoken, concrete
presentation.music: continuous background score with ducking, intro/outro, and chapter stingers

narration.text: [solemn]Look closely: Bound captives and Spanish violence. This later engraving is not eyewitness evidence. It is an accusation aimed at an empire. [beat]Now imagine it entered as evidence and the empire itself became the defendant. Valladolid, [date:1550]. Before either side speaks, decide: just war or imperial crime?

narration.text: [fast]Your verdict needs three tests. [emphasis]First:[/emphasis] reconstruct Sepúlveda's argument. [emphasis]Second:[/emphasis] test Las Casas as witness and participant. [emphasis]Third:[/emphasis] compare the chamber's argument with colonial consequences.[/fast] [beat]Argument. Witness. Consequence.

animation.title: THE JURY'S THREE TESTS
los: Test Las Casas as a witness
Judge the debate by its consequences

narration.text: [solemn]For conquest: Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda, a scholar who never crossed the Atlantic. His case was a chain. [VOICE:sepulveda][fierce]Aristotle taught that some peoples are natural slaves. Human sacrifice proves grave wrongdoing. Wrongdoing can justify war. War opens the way for Spanish government and Christian teaching. [VOICE:host][beat]Follow the logic. The next exhibit tests every link.

scenes.production_notes: Build the argument as a causal chain. The learner must see how one premise authorizes the next before the evidence tests it.

narration.text: [solemn]Now the direction reverses. Bartolomé de las Casas had spent decades in Spanish America. The men did not debate face to face; each presented separately. [beat]Sepúlveda offered authority and logic. Las Casas answered with experience, Indigenous rationality, and violence committed under Spanish rule.

animation.title: TEST THE CLAIM AGAINST THE SYSTEM

narration.text: [VOICE:lascasas][fierce]They are not tools for another people's profit. They reason, govern, worship, and form political communities. [VOICE:host][solemn]Inspect the system. This later Potosí engraving is not eyewitness evidence from Valladolid, but it sharpens Las Casas's question: can coerced labor and silver extraction be renamed civilization?

scenes.production_notes: Treat the engraving as a source to inspect, not wallpaper. Labels identify the system while narration explicitly limits the image's evidentiary role.

But it visualizes the accusation at the center of his case: Spain called violence moral instruction, while its victims experienced domination.

device_params.question: Can a coherent argument survive evidence of its consequences?

narration.text: [solemn]You are on the panel. Sepúlveda's argument depends on judging another people inferior. Las Casas brings experience and evidence, but he is not morally innocent. [beat]Can conquest survive the consequences produced in its name? [pause:2]Choose before history answers.

scenes.production_notes: Evidence cards face off rather than hero portraits. Hold two seconds with no camera movement and sharply ducked music so the learner must decide.

narration.text: [solemn]History refuses the clean ending. The panel announced [emphasis]no official verdict[/emphasis]. The dispute remained unresolved, and scholars still debate its policy effects. [pause:1]But outside the chamber, Spanish domination and coerced labor continued. The empty room is not neutrality. Compare the arguments with the outcome.

scenes.production_notes: Pull away from the empty chamber. A single low thud marks the missing verdict; the score then drops out before the ground-truth sentence.

animation.title: JUDGE THE DEBATE BY ITS CONSEQUENCES

narration.text: [solemn]Put the chamber beside the colony. Valladolid made conquest answer a sustained moral argument. It produced no official verdict, and it did not dismantle the coercive institutions of empire. [beat]That distinction matters for the exam: an argument can expose a contradiction without immediately changing power. Intellectual significance does not equal immediate social change.

scenes.production_notes: Return to the mine under a causal diagram. The image supplies ground truth while the diagram distinguishes intellectual significance from immediate change.

source.notes: Later illustration of colonial mining used to represent continuing coercive institutions.
source.title: Indigenous workers in a mine at Potosí, Upper Peru

narration.text: [solemn]Now test the witness. Earlier, Las Casas supported importing enslaved Africans while trying to relieve Indigenous suffering. He later repudiated that position and recognized the same right to freedom. [beat]This does not erase his Indigenous defense, and that defense does not erase his earlier harm. Moral witness is not moral innocence.

animation.prompt: A living historical engraving of a sixteenth-century European council chamber in session. Paper edges stir subtly, candles flicker, and faint dust drifts through shafts of light. Keep the camera static. Do not morph or add or remove or change any content.

narration.text: [refrain]Remember the pattern: power makes a claim, evidence tests it, and consequences expose what it hides.[/refrain] Valladolid did not invent human rights or end conquest. [beat]Its narrower significance: within an empire, conquest had to answer a moral challenge. On the exam, separate an argument's importance from its immediate effects.
